summary: Iteration 42 — Verified FAL_API_KEY fix resolves the Kokoro voiceover 401 in the render pipeline. Also end-to-end verified the Pre-render Timeline Editor (POST /studio/render/preview → POST /studio/render with preview_id) works and produces a real R2-hosted final MP4. Backend logs confirm every Kokoro POST since the key swap returns 200 OK. Test1 (direct /studio/render) hit a SEPARATE downstream failure (0 stock clips for a 1-scene short script) that is unrelated to the voiceover bug.

minor.issue: Very short 3-sentence scripts collapse to a single scene inside the direct render path, and if Pexels returns 0 results for that beat's search_query the render fails with 'Could not resolve any scene visuals (Flux/stock both empty).' The /studio/render/preview path (same script) instead split the same text into 3 scenes and all 3 fetched stock cleanly. Recommend either (a) enforce a min_beats=2 floor inside /studio/render's beat splitter to match the preview path, or (b) add a per-scene retry with a broader search_query fallback when the primary stock query returns 0 results. Not related to the FAL_API_KEY / voiceover bug.

action_items: None required for the voiceover bug — the fix is verified.

Optional (not blocking): harden /studio/render beat-splitting or stock-search fallback so ultra-short scripts don't collapse to 1 scene + fail when Pexels returns 0 results. Preview path is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: The direct /studio/render path uses different beat-splitting semantics than /studio/render/preview for the same script. Preview produced 3 scenes; direct produced 1. If Charity's users often paste 2-3 sentence scripts, this asymmetry means the preview flow is dramatically more reliable than the classic flow. Consider unifying on _target_beat_count_from_words + split_script_into_beats(min_beats=2) in both endpoints.

_poll_render terminal-state check: render docs use status='complete' (not 'completed'). Any admin/monitoring code that only checks 'completed' would misclassify successful jobs. Fixed in the test but worth grepping for elsewhere.
